name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.325.0 — An executed repro answers the reject: the disposer's return gains an optional repro field ({ command, observed }) on a reject it grounded in a command it actually ran, and a host's new policy.stops.rejectWithEvidence (accept by default, ask to bring the question back) lets --mark dispositions accept such a reject itself with one vetoable Auto-picked line; a waive and a repro-less reject still go to the user. /spec:fanout --ask accepts rejectWithEvidence. The grounding contract's Policy block gains the key, so hosts are flagged stale once. 7.324.0 — a fan-out lane's exit survives the sidecar delete its own step prints: the exit is also recorded beside the lane's delegation marker, and the fan-out reads it there first (q28). 7.323.0 — Predictable stops become host policy: a new policy.stops block in the host config (repairRound, buildEscalate, reviewEscalate, redFindings, prototypeClose), written with safe defaults, answers the review repair round, build and review escalations and critical-tier red findings with a printed vetoable auto-pick shared by solo runs and lanes; deleting a prototype stays a question by default. The fan-out's PREFLIGHT standing sheet is retired (--ask <key> relays a stop for one run), and /spec:fix no longer asks before committing a dirty tree — /git:commit's own approvals are the stop.
